clue.text: Meeting class outside university

indicators.note: to be outside something is to wrap around it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: a form is a school class
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A seminar held off campus, away from the university buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: FORM, the British school word for a class, goes round U.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum is a gathering or assembly held for open discussion, which makes it a kind of meeting.

clue.text: Draw attention to workers that will keep up standards

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing in for a noun

blocks.note: to flag something is to point it out
the staff are the workers of an organisation

explanation.surface: A manager singling out employees who maintain quality.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads standards as quality levels, but a standard is also a flag or banner.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagpole physically holds a banner aloft, and a standard is a ceremonial banner, so it literally keeps one up.

clue.text: Step right up and go over

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a pace is a single step
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A fairground barker inviting people to step up and have a go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Step right up' sounds like a showman's cry; PACE then R is written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to summarise points already made, which is going over them again briefly.

clue.text: Ordered, trim and neat for strict disciplinarian

indicators.note: things that have been ordered have been arranged, so these letters are put into a fresh sequence

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drill sergeant demanding everything be orderly, trim and neat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like it describes the tidy state the disciplinarian demands, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A martinet is someone who insists on rigid obedience to rules, named after a French army drillmaster.

clue.text: Luxurious City bar is demolished

indicators.note: a demolished building is knocked down and its material can be rebuilt in another shape

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plush bar in the City of London being torn down.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, and 'Luxurious' at the front is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sybaritic describes self-indulgent love of pleasure, after the ancient Greek city Sybaris, famous for opulent living.

clue.text: Literary poet showing lots of ostentation

indicators.note: lots of something is most but not all of it, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: swank is showy display; its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A flamboyant writer famous for showing off.
explanation.walkthrough: SWANK, slang for showing off, loses its K. Shakespeare was called the Swan of Avon, and poets were literary swans.
explanation.definitionFit: In literary usage a swan is a poet, the bird being sacred to Apollo and supposed to sing sweetly before death.

clue.text: Charitable payment to the sick reduced to small coin

indicators.note: something reduced has been cut short, so the tail end is clipped off

blocks.note: sickness benefit is a state payment; its last letter is cut
a cent is a coin of low value

explanation.surface: Sick pay so meagre it has been whittled down to pennies.
explanation.walkthrough: BENEFIT loses its T, then CENT follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Beneficent means doing good or showing active kindness, which is what a charitable person does.

clue.text: Delight in artist with power over hearts

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician
vis is Latin for force or power
H is the card-suit abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: Taking pleasure in a painter whose work wins people's hearts.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' simply puts VIS above H. VIS for power is the Latin word, known from phrases like vis viva.
explanation.definitionFit: To ravish someone is to fill them with intense delight or enchant them.

clue.text: Tons cutting outside income contributing to government revenue

indicators.note: a word placed outside another wraps around it on both sides

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for tons
axing is cutting
pay is earned income

explanation.surface: Massive cuts made to earnings that feed the Treasury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' looks like it describes the tons; it is a separate word wrapped around the income, after the single letter for tons.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxpaying means handing over money owed to the state, which is how a citizen funds public income.

clue.text: Pioneer studying radiation remedy involving iodine

indicators.note: to involve something is to include it within, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: a cure is a remedy
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A scientist working on radiation treatment that uses iodine.
explanation.walkthrough: CURE holds I; radioactive iodine really is a medical treatment, which helps the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie Curie did founding research on radioactivity and won Nobel prizes in physics and chemistry.

clue.text: Arsenic? Sure to suss out

blocks.note: As is the chemical symbol for arsenic
certain means sure

explanation.surface: A detective confident they can establish that arsenic was the poison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arsenic' with its question mark looks like the thing being investigated; it only supplies its chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain is to find something out for certain, and suss out is informal for working out the truth.

clue.text: Change mind about cross person that’s annoying

indicators.note: one thing about another is placed around it

blocks.note: to veer is to change direction or opinion
X is a cross

explanation.surface: Reconsidering one's view of an irritating, bad-tempered person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' wants to mean angry, describing the person; here it is the letter shaped like a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: A vexer is one who vexes, that is, someone who irritates or troubles others.

clue.text: Infected doubter dismissing Covid initially

indicators.note: dismissing someone sends them away, so a letter is removed
initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: a sceptic doubts things
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Covid denier who catches the virus after all.
explanation.walkthrough: SCEPTIC loses its first C.
explanation.definitionFit: A septic wound is one contaminated with bacteria, so it is infected.

clue.text: Staff go moving around back of theatre not visible to audience

indicators.note: things moving around change position, so the letters are rearranged
the back of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: Stagehands bustling about backstage, out of the audience's sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff go' reads as a command to the crew, but those words plus the last letter of theatre are the raw material to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Offstage means in the wings, out of view of the spectators watching a play.

clue.text: Utter guile — the art of politicians

blocks.note: to utter is to say or state
craft is cunning or guile

explanation.surface: A cynic's view that politics is nothing but complete cunning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like an adjective meaning complete; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Statecraft is the skill of managing government affairs, the craft practised by statesmen.

clue.text: Trainee programme opened up by Institution of Civil Engineers

blocks.note: an app is a computer program
rent is the past participle of rend, to tear open
ICE is the abbreviation for the institution

explanation.surface: An engineering institution launching a scheme for trainees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opened up' reads as launched; it is RENT, torn open.
explanation.definitionFit: An apprentice learns a trade while working under a skilled employer, which is a trainee.

clue.text: Plane curves from airborne fighter with missiles in South America

blocks.note: a para is a paratrooper
bolas are weighted cords thrown by South American gauchos

explanation.surface: A jet fighter's flight path as it fires missiles over South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' suggests an aircraft, but it is the geometry sense: a flat surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A parabola is a conic section, a curve lying in a single flat geometric surface.

clue.text: Riddle mostly over hospital for doctors and nurses perhaps?

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is lost
turned over means flipped, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: to riddle is to sift through a sieve; the T goes
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A hospital puzzle involving its medical staff.
explanation.walkthrough: A riddle is a coarse sieve, so to riddle is to sift. The question mark flags definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The doctorfish and the nurse shark are sea creatures, so medical job titles here name marine species.

clue.text: Chap is after part of London common

indicators.note: being after something means following it, setting the order of the parts

blocks.note: Hackney is a London borough
Ed is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man living on a piece of London common land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Common' looks like a noun, a London park; it is the adjective meaning trite.
explanation.definitionFit: Hackneyed phrases are overused and stale, so they are common in the sense of commonplace and banal.

clue.text: Deluge came down as many matches are played

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing in for an adjective

blocks.note: a deluge is a flood
to light is to land, as a bird alights

explanation.surface: Torrential rain falling while football fixtures go ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: LIT for came down is the old sense of light, to land or settle, as in alight.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening sports fixtures are staged under powerful lamps, so the stadium is brightly illuminated.

clue.text: Crossing over a period of days

blocks.note: for a time means over that time
D is the abbreviation for days

explanation.surface: A journey that took several days to complete.
explanation.walkthrough: FOR means over in phrases like 'for a week', and D is the dictionary abbreviation for days.
explanation.definitionFit: A ford is a shallow place in a river where people or vehicles can wade to the other bank.

clue.text: Reviewed the cooling of human culture

indicators.note: to review is to look at afresh, so the letters are seen in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A critic writing about how a civilisation's culture went cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reviewed' suggests a critic's write-up, but it is the signal to rearrange THE COOLING.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethnology is the comparative study of peoples and their customs, so the adjective relates to societies' ways of life.

clue.text: Mistakes noted during Canberra talks

indicators.note: something happening during an event sits within it, so the letters lie inside the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the boundary between these two words

explanation.surface: Errors recorded at diplomatic talks in Australia's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across canbERRA TAlks.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are listed corrections of printing errors, which are mistakes formally recorded in a book.

clue.text: Book (classical) virtuoso pianist

blocks.note: liber is the Latin word for book
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: Booking a classical virtuoso for a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classical' here means in Latin, the language of classical Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberace was a flamboyant American entertainer famous for showy keyboard performances in Las Vegas.

clue.text: Like one’s brain’s evolutionary design at the front?

definitions.text: Like one’s brain’s evolutionary design at the front?

indicators.note: the front of each word is where its opening letter sits

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: Wondering how evolution shaped the forepart of the human brain.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: a brain has frontal lobes.
explanation.definitionFit: The brain is divided into rounded sections, including frontal ones at its forward end.

clue.text: Corrupt chamber is concerning

blocks.note: a po is a chamber pot
taken as written
on means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A worrying sign that a legislature has gone bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chamber' suggests a parliament; it is the chamber pot.
explanation.definitionFit: To poison minds or institutions is to corrupt them morally with a harmful influence.

clue.text: Sudden inundation’s well over western parts of Tewkesbury

indicators.note: the western side of a word written left to right is its opening end

blocks.note: a spa is a mineral spring or well
the two leading letters of the town

explanation.surface: Floodwater rising over the west side of a riverside town.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts SPA above. Tewkesbury, a Gloucestershire town at the meeting of two rivers, is notorious for flooding.
explanation.definitionFit: A river in spate is in sudden heavy flood, and a spate is a rush of water.

clue.text: Spotted deer unknown in Asia, mostly running

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all, so the final letter is lost
running about, the letters scatter and settle into a new order

blocks.note: X is an unknown in algebra
the continent with its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: A rare deer sighted on the move somewhere in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: X goes in with ASI and the four letters are then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The axis, or chital, is a white-dotted Indian species of the deer family.

clue.text: Raft beginning to sink in Welsh lake

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter
one thing in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: Bala is the largest natural lake in Wales
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A raft starting to go under on a lake in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Bala Lake, or Llyn Tegid, is in north Wales; S sits inside it before the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light wood, and a balsa is a raft built from it, as used in South America.

clue.text: A university eleven complain bitterly over unknown supporter

indicators.note: turned over means flipped end to end, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university
XI is eleven in Roman numerals, and a cricket team
to rail is to protest angrily
Y is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: A college team grumbling bitterly about an anonymous fan.
explanation.walkthrough: An eleven is a cricket or football team, written XI; RAIL is turned over to LIAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An auxiliary gives help or backup to others, which makes it a helper or supporter.

clue.text: One showing some French skill in beginnings of “cogito ergo sum”?

definitions.text: One showing some French skill in beginnings of “cogito ergo sum”?

indicators.note: the beginning of each word is its opening letter
one thing in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: des is French for some
art is skill
the opening letter of each Latin word

explanation.surface: Praising a French philosopher's skill in coining a famous Latin maxim.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: the French thinker wrote cogito ergo sum, I think therefore I am, and the skill sits among its initials.
explanation.definitionFit: René Descartes, the French philosopher, coined this Latin saying, and the wordplay itself shows a Frenchman at work.

clue.text: Press down? Nothing’s left to peruse

indicators.note: something that has left has departed, so a letter goes away

blocks.note: O looks like zero, nothing
to peruse is to read; the whole phrase is kept

explanation.surface: A journalist told to stop the presses because there is no news left to read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like remaining; it means gone, so O leaves TO READ.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread is to step on something and crush or flatten it underfoot.
